So the reference under `.claude/reference` doesn't show these edits yet, and nothing has checked them. Please run `piton build` on the host before the code step.

**Likely cause (a guess: I can't see the code or a failing run).** Questions now always run in a container. When a project opens, they carry on the latest question conversation saved with it, and that session was most likely recorded when questions still ran on the host. The questions' container volume doesn't have that session, so `claude -p --resume <id>` (or `--fork-session`) fails at once. A failed run never records a new session, so every later ask retries the same dead session ID and fails again. The app then shows only a generic "the harness reported an error", which hides Claude Code's real message ("No conversation found…").

The coding agent should first confirm this from the actual error output before relying on it.

**What I changed in `spec/scope/harness-integration/index.pi`**
- **`HarnessIntegrationShape.context`**, rewritten where it said "if one can't be carried on, the next request starts a new one":
  - Questions only carry on a conversation started in the questions' volume. They never resume one saved from host-run questions, or one whose session the volume no longer has.
  - A request whose conversation can't be carried on is never failed for that reason, and never retried on the same conversation. This covers the harness saying there's no such session (Claude Code's "No conversation found") and a conversation started elsewhere.
  - Instead, the same prompt is sent again at once as a new conversation with no context. The dead conversation is never tried again by any later request, including through the project's history.
  - A question re-sent this way is recorded and shown as starting a new conversation, with the "New conversation" divider in `AskConversationScope`.
- **New `HarnessIntegrationShape.failures`**:
  - A failed run always says what went wrong in the harness's own words: its result error or streamed error events, otherwise its stderr and exit status, quoted as written.
  - A task shows this in its output; a question shows it at the end of its answer.
  - "The harness reported an error" may only appear as a heading above what the harness said, never on its own.
  - A run that couldn't be started says why, and one Podman couldn't run defers to `ContainerEnvironmentScope.podmanAccess` from the last step.
- I added an import of `AskConversationScope` to that file.
- I wrote the understanding file at `.suspense/history/1791040980-HarnessErrorOnEveryAsk.understanding.md`.

**Anchors the code should follow**
- `HarnessIntegrationShape.context`: questions resume only sessions from their own volume, and a failed resume is re-sent once as a new conversation, after which that session is never used again.
- `HarnessIntegrationShape.failures`: show the harness's actual error.
- `AskConversationScope` (the New Conversation and Answers sections): mark the re-sent question as a new conversation, and end a failed answer with the error.
- `ContainerEnvironmentScope.podmanAccess` (from the previous step): name Podman, not the harness, when Podman can't run the container.

49:#### Context
50-
51-The harness keeps its context between requests instead of starting fresh each time. Each lane of the [PromptSendingScope](../prompt-mode/sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) carries on a conversation of its own, so nothing a task of one lane read reaches a task of the other: the spec lane's, carried on by Spec tasks and a Chain prompt's spec steps, and the code lane's, carried on by Code tasks, a Chain prompt's code step, and Freeform tasks. Each task sent carries on its own lane's, and since a lane runs one task at a time, two tasks never carry on the same conversation at once. A Chain prompt's steps hand on to each other as text, the prompt and what the step before replied, as the [ModeSystemPromptsScope](../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts-scope) says, so the handoff crosses lanes whatever each lane's conversation holds. When the project is opened, each lane carries on the latest conversation among its own tasks in the history, a Chain task by the lane of the step it was.
52-A run in a container keeps its lane's sessions in that lane's volume, and a run on the host where the harness keeps them on the host, as the [ContainerEnvironmentScope](../container-environment/index.md#container-environment-scope) says, so a conversation is only carried on where it began: turning the project's "Run code tasks in a container" option on or off starts the code lane on a new conversation at its next task.
53-Questions from the Ask tab share a separate conversation of their own, and when the project is opened they carry on the latest conversation among the questions saved with it. A question asked while another is running carries on a copy of that conversation, so questions running at the same time never write over each other. A conversation is only carried on in the project it began in, each open project keeping its own tasks' and questions' conversations while it is in the background. Questions run in a container, so a question carries on only a conversation begun in the questions' volume, never one saved from a question asked on the host before questions ran in containers, nor one whose session that volume no longer holds.
54-A request whose conversation can't be carried on, because the harness says it has no such session, as Claude Code's "No conversation found", or because it was begun elsewhere, is never failed for it, and never retried on the same conversation: it is sent again at once as a new conversation, the same prompt, with no context, and the conversation it couldn't carry on is not tried again by any later request, the project's history included. A question sent again so is recorded and shown as starting a new conversation, as the [AskConversationScope](../prompt-mode/ask-conversation/index.md#ask-conversation-scope) marks one. Each run applies its own prompt's systemPrompt, even when it carries on a conversation begun in a different mode. The palette's file search always starts fresh.
55-A conversation can be left for a new one, from the chat input's New conversation button, as the [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) says, which leaves the conversation of the lane it is used for: the next request in it starts a new conversation with no context, and the one left is not carried on again, not by a run of it still going, nor by the project's history. Leaving it is kept with the project, as the [ProjectDataScope](../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope) says, so a project opened after a lane's or the questions' conversation was left starts a new one there too, rather than carrying on the latest conversation in its history, until a run after the reset begins one of its own. How much context a conversation holds is known from what the harness reports with each reply: everything the model was given, cached or not, and what it wrote, as of its latest reply; replies of subagents don't count.
--

content.text:
Your asks should work again: when a question can't carry on its old conversation, it's now sent again straight away as a new one instead of failing. Everything passes: all 101 prompt-mode tests at 4 threads, and the full suite of 469 at 2 threads. In the last two full runs at 4 threads, one sidebar test (`referenced_spec_shows_the_understanding`) failed both times, though it passes alone and in those other runs. It's the same timing-sensitive test that failed now and then before, and my change doesn't touch that sidebar. I haven't tried it in the real app yet.

**What was wrong:** the failed ask saved in `.suspense/asks/1791040914-ContainerPerProject.json` shows it. Questions now run in a container, but they were still resuming the conversation saved from when they ran on the host. Claude Code in the container doesn't have it, so it printed "No conversation found with session ID: b0b1d74a-…" and returned an error result with no text. The app showed that as "The harness reported an error". Because a failed run never recorded a new conversation, every later ask tried the same one and failed the same way.
